clue.text: Deprive of wind, but remain unflustered

definitions.meaning: to leave a sailing ship stuck with no breeze in its sails
read as two words, to stay composed and untroubled

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words: BE plus CALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship left without wind is stranded, and staying unruffled is keeping one's composure.

clue.text: He atones for former policemen initially fomenting a riot

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of policemen
fomenting stirs up the letters of a riot

explanation.surface: A man makes amends for ex-officers who first stirred up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fomenting' scrambles A RIOT into IATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes amends or expiation for a wrong is making atonement.

clue.text: First-class porter carrying 20 in Yorkshire

indicators.note: carrying says the first-class letters and the beer hold something between them

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
20 points to the answer at 20 across, a colour, and red is one

explanation.surface: A top-notch railway porter lugs something through Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' refers to 20 across, COLOUR; RED is a colour. 'porter' is beer, not a railway worker.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the valley of the River Aire, a dale lying within that county, and also a terrier breed named after it.

clue.text: Shabby woman in Holy Writ imprisoned by soldiers

indicators.note: imprisoned by says the soldiers enclose everything else

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: in says the woman's name goes inside the scripture letters

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of Holy Writ
Thea is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A down-at-heel woman from the Bible is locked up by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned by' and 'in' are the two container signals. 'woman in Holy Writ' looks like a biblical character such as Eve, but the woman is just any name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes eaten by moths are full of holes and look worn and threadbare.

clue.text: A north country person caught one in the Tiber valley

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the upper Tiber flows through Umbria in central Italy, so a native there is an Umbrian

explanation.surface: Someone from northern England is spotted in an Italian river valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' looks like I, but the whole phrase 'one in the Tiber valley' is a person from Umbria. Cumbria is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is a county of northern England, so its natives are north-country folk.

clue.text: Writer whose work is in Rochester? Quite the contrary

definitions.text: Writer whose work is in Rochester? Quite the contrary

parts.words: Writer whose work is in Rochester? Quite the contrary
parts.note: Rochester could be the Kent city, but he is the hero of a famous novel, so he is in her work rather than her work being in him

explanation.surface: An author whose writings are held in the city of Rochester.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Rochester is the brooding master of Thornfield in Jane Eyre; 'Quite the contrary' reverses the relation.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the Victorian novelist who wrote Jane Eyre, in which Edward Rochester appears.

clue.text: Black sack carried after burning rubbish here

indicators.note: after says the word for sack comes behind the other letters

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
something carried or worn is on, as with a coat on
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: A black bin bag is taken away after rubbish has been burned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a bin bag, but it is the verb, FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor fire built to dispose of garden waste is where rubbish is burnt.

clue.text: One dined in it at first, being a novice

indicators.note: at first says the words in and it come at the front

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one
to have dined is to have eaten

explanation.surface: Someone eats inside an establishment for the first time as a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' is the placement signal: it puts the words 'in it' ahead of the rest, rather than meaning a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly admitted member who is just beginning is a beginner.

clue.text: Anonymous male blunders into loch

indicators.note: into says the jumbled letters go inside the loch

parts.note: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

indicators.note: blunders suggests the letters of male stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: An unnamed man stumbles into a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunders' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container. A loch is a Scottish lake, and this one is famous for its monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no known name is to be unidentified.

clue.text: Less than threepence for this musical work?

definitions.text: Less than threepence for this musical work?

parts.words: Less than threepence for this musical work?
parts.note: plays on Brecht and Weill's Threepenny Opera: something smaller than that opera would be a little one

explanation.surface: A bargain-price ticket for a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Threepence was an old British coin; the clue hints at The Threepenny Opera, and the answer is literally a small opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, short opera with spoken dialogue is a diminutive form of opera.

clue.text: Enfeebled businessman's situation?

definitions.meaning: weak and frail, as in old age
read as two words, a businessman is employed inside a company

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as IN FIRM, where a businessman works; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A frail, weakened person lacks physical strength.

clue.text: Composer left holding bandleader's instrument

indicators.note: holding says the composer and the L clasp another letter between them

parts.note: George Frideric Handel, the composer of Messiah
the leading letter of band

explanation.surface: A composer abandons the musical instrument belonging to the leader of a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb meaning abandoned but is just L. 'bandleader's' gives the first letter of band.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bell rung by hand is a musical instrument played in sets by ringers.

clue.text: One originally acting in charge of a son or daughter

indicators.note: in says the preceding letters go inside the word for charge

parts.note: to charge a glass is to fill it
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of acting

explanation.surface: A single person temporarily put in charge of somebody's child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' reads as one phrase meaning responsible, but 'in' is the container signal and 'charge' means FILL. I plus A go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes the duty or relationship a child owes to a parent.

clue.text: Trite remark abandoned by leading character in play

indicators.note: the word for trite remark is left by its leading letter, so its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a hackneyed, overused saying is a platitude

explanation.surface: A clichéd line is cut by the star actor in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is the definition, in the sense of freedom of movement, not a stage drama; 'leading character' is the first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Play in a rope or a rule means room to move, which is scope or freedom.

clue.text: He reduces rubbish transported uphill

indicators.note: in a down clue uphill means the letters run upwards, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
something transported by cart has been carted

explanation.surface: A man cuts down waste that has been hauled up a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: ROT plus CARTED reads, in reverse, as the answer, because 'uphill' turns a down answer bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic who belittles or disparages someone diminishes their reputation.

clue.text: A swimmer turning back in Lake Frome

indicators.note: turning back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A swimmer turns round in an Australian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run E FRO across 'Lake Frome', which is reversed. Lake Frome is a salt lake in South Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a freshwater fish of the carp family, often golden, so it swims.

clue.text: Extremely bad course possibly made unintelligible

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way
extremely picks the first and last letters of bad

explanation.surface: A really poor course might have been rendered confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely bad' looks like an intensifier but gives B and D, which are mixed with COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden or clouded over has been made hard to understand.

clue.text: Charlie's better — it's in the paper

parts.note: a charlie is a fool in British slang, so Charlie's is fool's
to cap a story is to better it

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie is outdone, and it is reported in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is British slang for a fool, not a name. 'it's in the' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional size of writing sheet, named after a jester watermark.

clue.text: Gulls in hawks' cages

definitions.meaning: falconers' enclosures where hawks are kept while moulting

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense also gives the London word for stable lanes; here it is the falconry one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mew is an old name for a seabird of the gull family, and mews were buildings housing moulting falcons.

clue.text: Dance preceded by suitable-sounding food

indicators.note: preceded by says the dance comes after the other part
sounding says the word for suitable is heard, not spelt

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or suitable
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Before a dance there is food that seems appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: MEET (suitable, as in 'it is meet and right') sounds like MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ball of minced flesh is a dish one eats.

clue.text: Boarding an old wagon on payment

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the wagon above the payment

parts.note: wain is an archaic word for a farm wagon
scot is an old tax or payment, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard an old cart once the fare is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boarding' looks like getting on a vehicle, but it is wooden panelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden panelling on the lower part of a room's walls is a form of boarding.

clue.text: Union leaders decide to agitate

parts.note: the leading letters of the word union
to settle a question is to decide it

explanation.surface: Trade union bosses make up their minds to stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union leaders' looks like trade union bosses, but it gives the two opening letters of union.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to disturb or upset them, which is to agitate them.

clue.text: Seizer of power quietly /accommodated by Shylock?

indicators.note: accommodated by says the letter for quietly is housed inside the moneylender

parts.note: Shylock is the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, a usurer
P, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A power grabber is quietly housed by a moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock lends at interest, which makes him a usurer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who takes a throne or office without right grabs control illegitimately.

clue.text: Firm frown makes us blush

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to lour, or lower, is to scowl

explanation.surface: A stern scowl from a company boss leaves us red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes us' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To flush pink in the face with embarrassment is to redden.

clue.text: Organist harmed by such severe criticism

indicators.note: harmed suggests the letters of organist are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: A church musician is hurt by harsh reviews of a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ORGANIST gives the answer, the 'such' tying the criticism back to the harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe dressing-down or slating is informally called this.

clue.text: Opportune to include City in plan of action

indicators.note: to include says the word for opportune takes in the letters for City

parts.note: the time is ripe when it is opportune
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A timely idea to bring the financial district into a strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the postal district covering the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instructions for cooking, or for achieving something, is a method or formula.

clue.text: Bird which follows a character to church

indicators.note: follows says the word for which comes after the Greek letter

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns

explanation.surface: A bird trails some person on the way to a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a character' is a letter, here the Greek nu.
explanation.definitionFit: This small tree-climbing songbird cracks nuts by wedging them in bark.

clue.text: Exile finds haven in river quarter

indicators.note: in says the word for haven sits inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a port is a safe haven for ships
E, east, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: An outcast finds shelter in some district beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' looks like a district, but it is a compass point, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone expelled from a country is a banished person.

clue.text: Tell of military men no longer alive

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Recount stories of soldiers who have died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount or narrate a story is to tell it.
